text.p: Pioner International Ltd said on Friday it expected group profitability for the year to June 30, 1997 to be below the 1995/96 year.
Pioneer said the 1996/97 first quarter performance of its core building materials business was close to record results of the corresponding quarter in the 1995/96 (July-June) year.

"Overall, the performance of our core building materials business was close to the record results of the corresponding quarter last year," chairman David Hoare told shareholders at the annual meeting.

"During the first quarter of this financial year, European earnings exceeded expectations, as construction activity caught up on the backlog caused by the severe winter but were below last years results," Hoare said.
"In Asia, earnings were substantially higher than the pervious year, with especially strong performances from Hong Kong, Thailand and Malaysia," he said.

He said the Australian concrete and quarry performance also exceeded expectations with good construction activity in Queensland, New South Wales and Western Australia, but were also slightly behind last year.
Hoare said earnings from the United States were similiar to last year with Texas operations being hampered by wet weather.
Hoare said building products results in Australia continued to be impacted by depressed levels of housing starts and by wet weather in most states but there are some signs of improvements.

"Ampol's results were well below expectations, with a substantial reduction in profitability for the quarter, mainly because of depressed petrol refiner margins caused by surplus fuel supplies in the Asia Pacific region," Hoare said.

Hoare said retail margins were very competitive with new importers starting to supply to the independent sector in Sydney and Melbourne. Ampol is a 50/50 joint venture between Pioneer and Caltex Australia Ltd.
"For the group as a whole we expect profitablity for in the current year to be materially below last year's record results," Hoare said.
He said the outlook for the rest of the year is mixed. "In Europe we expect underlying economic conditions to be difficult and it will not be easy to match last years results."
Hoare said he expects the performance from its Israeli operations to be similiar to last year.
Australian conceretes and quarry operations of forecast to further reduce operating costs and should achieve price rises in some markets, Hoare said.
He said the Australian building products business is likely to have another difficult year with some improvements forecast in the housing industry during 1997.
"Asian operations should achieve significiantly higher earnings than last year," Hoare said.
He said the performance in Hong Kong would further improve. Thailand and Malaysia earnings would increase substantially as construction activity continues to expand.
The outlook for Singapore remained strong. However, China results were unlikely to improve and Vietnam was still having some start up problems. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
